cause.seoDescription: How can we make the world a little better? Local production, our grandmothers, sustainable tourism and inspiring others: the four things we care about most at Lobitos Ponchos.
cause.title:
How can we
make the world
a little better?
cause.lead: We know we can’t change the whole world at once. But we believe that if each of us changes a little of what’s around us, together, over time, we can make a big difference.
cause.intro: We’ve asked ourselves a lot about what we stand for and who we want to be. These are the four things that matter most to us:
indexItems: Close to home, kind to the earth

c1.title:
Close to home,
kind to the earth
c1.photoAlt: The Lobitos Ponchos stand on the beach with a sign that reads «Diseña tu propio Surf Poncho!» (Design your own surf poncho!)
c1.summary: We make every poncho right here in Lobitos, one at a time, made to last and with as little waste as possible.
c1.lead: So many people in Peru feel they have to leave for Lima to get ahead. We'd rather create opportunities right here at home.
c1.p1: Forget fast fashion: we'd rather make one piece you'll love for years than a pile you'll soon forget. Even our fabric scraps get a second life as pouches and other little treasures.
c1.p2: Even our fabric scraps get a second life as pouches and other little treasures.
c1.p3: We're still learning. Step by step, we want to use more sustainable materials and tread more lightly on the earth.
c1.collabLead: Have an idea? Know a material we could try?
c1.collabText: We're always happy to learn, and even happier to work together.

c2.title: Our grandmothers
c2.photoAlt: One of our grandmothers with a visitor, showing Lobitos Ponchos pouches in front of her sewing machine
c2.summary: Our grandmothers are the heart of Lobitos Ponchos. Every poncho they sew brings them an income of their own, and the pride of sharing a lifetime of skill.
c2.lead: Our elders have so much to give: their knowledge, their experience, and stories still waiting to be shared.
c2.p1: With Lobitos Ponchos, our grandmothers earn their own money from home, doing work they're proud of. That means more independence, real recognition for their craft, and more time with their grandsons, Kevyn and Iván.
c2.p2: And visitors now come all the way to their door to see how their poncho is made, sparking friendships that would never have happened otherwise.

c3.title: Sustainable tourism
c3.photoAlt: Local kids and visitors in ponchos on a fishing boat pulled up on the beach in Lobitos
c3.summary: We want visitors to know Lobitos beyond the beach, and to meet the families who call it home.
c3.lead: Too often, visitors move between their hotel, the beach and the usual sights without ever meeting the people who built this town.
c3.p1: Our ponchos open the door to village life: its families, its history, and a community that has lived from the sea for generations.
c3.highlight: We've already watched friendships grow between people from completely different worlds.

c4.title: Inspiring Others
c4.quote: Our biggest dream? That you'll see you can do it too.
c4.summary: We started with a few sewing machines, two grandmothers and a lot of heart. If we can do it, so can you.
c4.p1: Our team is young and old, from Lobitos and from far away, and we've learned that the most different people can build something beautiful together.
c4.p2: We hope our story inspires you to create, team up and back the local projects around you.
c4.photoAlt: Collage of young people from Lobitos

closing.title: Maybe the world changes one small place at a time.
closing.text: For us, it started right here in Lobitos. Where will it start for you?

team.seoDescription: The hands behind every piece: meet the grandmothers and young people of Lobitos who make each poncho by hand.
team.title:
The hands
behind
every piece
team.lead: Two grandmothers, their grandsons and a few friends from near and far, all believing in handmade work and the stories it carries.
team.closingTitle: Sewn with tradition. Made to last.

people.label: 01 — Founder
people.name: Esmérita "Mery" Eche Periche
people.bio: Esmérita is 70 and has lived in Lobitos all her life. She learned to sew from her mother as a young girl, and sewing has been part of her ever since. Today she brings a lifetime of experience to the workshop, shaping every piece with hands that have never stopped carrying tradition forward.

people.label: 02 — Master artisan
people.name: Irma Bancayan Eche
people.bio: Kevyn’s grandmother, born and raised in Lobitos. Irma has been sewing and making things by hand since she was 10. She finishes the edges and joins every piece together, giving each poncho its final shape before it’s checked and sent out.

people.label: 03 — Production
people.name: Kevyn Abad
people.bio: Born and raised in Lobitos, Kevyn studies Hospitality and Restaurant Management. He takes every order, measures customers, picks the color combinations, and cuts the fabric for his grandmothers. Then he checks each poncho and hands it over himself. His goal: to support his grandmothers and pay for his studies.

people.label: 04 — Co-founder · Marketing & strategy
people.name: Kerstin Ulrich "Tiíta"
people.bio: Born and raised in Switzerland to a Peruvian mother, Kerstin first came to Lobitos in 2018 to volunteer with Waves for Development, teaching English to the village teens, Kevyn and Ivan among them. Seeing how few opportunities there were once school ended, she co-founded Lobitos Ponchos with them. She studied medicine, speaks four languages and now lives in Lobitos, where she looks after the brand, the photos, social media and partnerships. When she can, she plays in a band. Above all, she’s proud to be part of a team that feels like family.

people.label: 05 — Admin & community
people.name: Ivan Vite
people.bio: Born and raised in Lobitos, Ivan is studying Environmental Engineering away from home. He keeps the admin side running smoothly, making sure every handmade piece is backed by order, care and community.

story.seoDescription: How Lobitos Ponchos began: a volunteer, two young locals and their seamstress grandmothers. Plus the story of Lobitos, from fishing cove to oil town to today’s surf village.
story.title:
Our
story
story.lead: Lobitos Ponchos is a family business. It grew out of a friendship, a few sewing machines and the wish to create opportunities without having to leave home.

chapters.title: A volunteer and two students
chapters.photoAlt: Young people from Lobitos in colorful ponchos
chapters.p1: In 2018, Tiíta (Kerstin) came to Lobitos to volunteer with the NGO Waves for Development. She taught English to the village teenagers, Kevyn and Ivan among them.
chapters.p2: Over the years, Tiíta saw how few opportunities young people had once they finished school. Teacher and students became friends, and later partners, built on trust and the wish to learn together.

chapters.title: 2022: the first poncho
chapters.photoAlt: One of our grandmothers with a visitor, in front of her sewing machine
chapters.p1: In 2022, Kevyn and Ivan, then 22, started making surf ponchos to pay for their studies. Tiíta joined in with marketing, photos and social media.
chapters.p2: The microfiber fabric is bought in Lima and cut in Lobitos. Then their grandmothers, Mery and Irma, sew it at home, so they can work at their own pace and spend more time with their grandsons. Every customer can choose their own colors.

chapters.title: Growing without losing ourselves
chapters.photoAlt: The Lobitos Ponchos stand at a market on the beach
chapters.p1: We started turning fabric offcuts into accessories: glasses cases, pencil cases, bum bags and fin covers. Less waste, and new ideas.
chapters.p2: Then came markets, our first business orders and a very special one: 35 ponchos for the Australian Embassy in Peru. And volunteers from all over the world came too, helping us with the website, social media and markets.

chapters.title: What we dream of
chapters.photoAlt: Local kids and visitors in ponchos on a fishing boat on the beach in Lobitos
chapters.p1: We want to grow without losing who we are: freedom, community, a simple life and a connection with the sea. We’d love to use ever more sustainable materials and bring more people from the village into the workshop.
chapters.p2: One day we want our own space in Lobitos: a shop, a workshop and a meeting place, where you can see how your poncho is made and meet the people who sew it.

story.townLead: Before the ponchos, before the surf, Lobitos already had plenty of stories to tell.
story.townPhotoAlt: A surfer on a Lobitos wave, with the oil platforms on the horizon

timeline.title: Fishing families
timeline.text: Lobitos began as a small cove of fishing families. Its name comes from the sea lions (lobos marinos) that came up onto the shore.

timeline.title: Oil
timeline.text: A lot of oil was found under the sand. The rights to it ended up in English hands, sold for very little.

timeline.title: The English arrive
timeline.text: With the Lobitos Oilfields company came Victorian-style wooden houses, the pier, the English Club, a cricket field and the casino, home to the town’s first cinema, said to be one of the first in South America.

timeline.title: War with Ecuador
timeline.text: The conflict with Ecuador brought the first army units to Lobitos.

timeline.title: The military
timeline.text: After the military coup, the government nationalized Peru’s oil: the army took over Talara and Lobitos, and the English had to leave. For decades, Lobitos was a military zone.

timeline.title: Heritage
timeline.text: The church, the old army headquarters and 21 historic houses were declared Cultural Heritage of the Nation.

timeline.title: A vibrant village
timeline.text: Lobitos is a small town of about a thousand people: calm, safe and full of life, with some of the best left-hand waves in Peru and a community of fishermen, surfers and families.

story.closingTitle: We’re still writing this story, together.
